name: HFS Provider-Level Medicaid Payment Data
dataType: Provider-level payments, patients served, average costs, adjustments
whyItMatters: Shows where Illinois Medicaid dollars flowed by provider, county, service category, and reporting year.
limitations: Aggregate provider-level data does not show full claim detail, patient-level acuity, managed care contract terms, or medical necessity context.
currentCoverage: The 2023 HFS Transparency Law provider file is parsed for hospital-type providers: 703 public payment rows are loaded, with 222 rows matched across 148 Illinois CMS hospital facilities.

name: HFS Fee Schedules Beyond Nursing Facilities
facilityType: Practitioner, DME, dental, therapy, transportation, pharmacy, FQHC/RHC, behavioral health, and related provider types
dataType: Published fee schedules and reimbursement policy files
whyItMatters: Builds the Medicaid reimbursement atlas behind professional, ancillary, clinic, drug, and transportation services.
limitations: Published fee schedules may not equal actual paid amounts after modifiers, prior authorization, managed care rules, denials, or policy exceptions.

name: Illinois Hospital Medicaid Rate Sheets
dataType: Hospital rate sheets and effective-date rate files
whyItMatters: Connects Illinois hospitals to Medicaid reimbursement logic instead of treating hospital quality data as a standalone layer.
limitations: Rate sheets need policy interpretation and may not capture managed care payments, claim edits, supplemental payments, or final settlement amounts.

name: Illinois Hospital Report Card API
dataType: Facility measures, values, quality, safety, patient experience, services, costs, and revenue signals
whyItMatters: Adds Illinois-specific quality, safety, staffing, service, cost, and revenue context around facility reimbursement.
limitations: Report card values are context and accountability signals; they do not prove reimbursement causation or full facility financial condition.

name: HFSRB Revenue, Expense, and Facility Inventory Data
agency: Illinois Health Facilities and Services Review Board
facilityType: Hospitals, ASTCs, ESRD, long-term care, and other regulated facilities
dataType: Beds, utilization, service lines, occupancy, revenue, expenses, and facility profiles
whyItMatters: Shows whether reimbursement signals align with capacity, occupancy, payer mix, services, and reported facility economics.
limitations: Report layouts vary by year and facility class; reported finance data still needs validation against cost reports and audited statements.

name: CMS HCRIS Cost Reports
facilityType: Hospitals, SNFs, home health, hospice, renal facilities, FQHC/RHC, CMHC, and other institutional providers
payer: Medicare with broader facility finance context
dataType: Cost reports, utilization, charges, Medicare settlement data, cost centers, and financial statement data
whyItMatters: Turns the project from rate lookup into facility finance analysis by exposing costs, charges, utilization, and settlement data.
limitations: Files are large and complex, require form-specific worksheet mapping, and reported costs are not the same as claim-level allowed amounts.
currentCoverage: Latest available CMS Hospital Provider Cost Report public-use API rows are attached for 207 Illinois hospital CCNs, giving the statewide leaderboard a facility economics layer beyond the original Taylorville proof row.

name: Medicare Utilization and Payment Public Use Files
facilityType: Physicians, suppliers, hospitals, outpatient departments, Part D prescribers, and other Medicare providers
dataType: Utilization, submitted charges, allowed amounts, Medicare payments, APC/DRG/service groupings
accessLevel: Public download and API-enabled CMS datasets
whyItMatters: Shows actual Medicare payment signals that can be compared against Illinois Medicaid rates and facility charges.
limitations: Public-use files are aggregated, privacy-suppressed where needed, and do not capture Medicare Advantage or full commercial payment behavior.

name: Inpatient DRG and LOS Rule Files
payer: Medicare IPPS benchmark and Medicaid DRG context
dataType: MS-DRG definitions, relative weights, diagnosis/procedure grouping logic, and length-of-stay benchmarks
whyItMatters: Explains how admission diagnosis, procedures, CC/MCC capture, discharge status, LOS, transfers, and outliers shape inpatient reimbursement.
limitations: Medicare IPPS logic is a benchmark; Illinois Medicaid and commercial inpatient reimbursement may use different DRG systems, weights, or contracts.

name: HAC, POA, Readmission, and Quality Penalty Data
dataType: Hospital-acquired condition measures, Present on Admission rules, readmission measures, penalties, and quality adjustment signals
accessLevel: Public CMS quality data and rules
whyItMatters: Shows how infections, pressure injuries, wounds, readmissions, and other quality events can create reimbursement loss or penalty exposure.
limitations: Penalty programs apply to specific payer/program rules and should be interpreted as prevention and documentation risk, not as a strategy to inflate claims.

name: Hospital Price Transparency Machine-Readable Files
payer: Commercial payer negotiated rates, cash prices, and gross charges
dataType: Machine-readable standard charges by item/service, billing code, payer/plan, gross charge, cash price, and negotiated-rate methodology
accessLevel: Public hospital website file, often CSV or JSON
whyItMatters: Shows public price and negotiated-rate signals that can be compared against reimbursement rules, service examples, and payer variation.
limitations: Files may exclude Medicare and Medicaid, can be huge or hard to parse, and do not prove paid claims, patient responsibility, volume, denials, or medical necessity.
currentCoverage: 10 Illinois hospital price-transparency sources are mapped in the starter basket; 7 parsed successfully into 996 normalized benchmark examples, with portal/error sources retained as evidence gaps.

name: Facility Careers Pages and Public Job Openings
agency: Facility websites, health-system career portals, and Illinois Hospital Report Card website fields
facilityType: Hospitals, nursing facilities, ASCs, and health-system operators
dataType: Facility homepage, careers page URL, hiring platform, job-opening count, clinical/non-clinical role mix, and observation date
whyItMatters: Open roles can reveal workforce demand, staffing pressure, service-line growth, and operating stress that reimbursement and quality files do not directly show.
limitations: Job counts change daily, may be duplicated across health-system portals, may cover multiple campuses, and do not prove actual vacancies, turnover, staffing ratios, or budgeted headcount.
